answer: Correlated-behavior bonds: each agent identity locks a refundable deposit that returns only after months of clean activity. Validators compare activity fingerprints, such as submission timing, gas sources and text embeddings. When one operator drives many accounts, they mirror each other like a single plume of smoke over a quiet ocean, and that cluster gets slashed together. Every fake costs a full deposit and only adds detection risk, so faking a crowd loses money.
